newsitem.title: JAPAN: Gajoen defers comment on reported note failure.
newsitem.headline: Gajoen defers comment on reported note failure.

text.p: Hotel operator Gajoen Kanko KK said on Tuesday it was looking into reports that it had failed to honour promissory notes and could not make an official comment until later, perhaps on Tuesday evening.

"We have yet to confirm whether we have failed to honour promissory notes as reported because we have not received any reports from senior executives in charge of this matter," a company official told Reuters.
"The company will hold an executive meeting in response to the situation and make an official comment as early as this evening," the official said.

Earlier, Japanese credit research company Teikoku Databank said in a report that Gajoen's transactions with banks had been suspended since January 6 after it failed to honour promissory notes for a second time.
A second failure to honour such notes is regarded in Japanese business practice as effectively a bankruptcy.
The company, which operates hotels and wedding halls, had debts totalling 9.88 billion yen, Teikoku Databank said.

It also said Gajoen would be the second company on the TSE's first section to fail this year after a chain of sushi restaurants, Kyotaru Co Ltd, made an insolvency filing in late January with debts of 101.3 billion yen.

Following the report, the Tokyo Stock Exchange announced that trade in Gajoen shares was being suspended for the whole of Tuesday's afternoon session. The shares, listed on the first section of the exchange, were last traded at 66 yen.
The shares were put under surveillance by the exchange in September after the hotel operator said that it had overdue taxes totalling about 13 billion yen.
